ACTION 23 OF 32 · PHASE 06

Secure the backend, accounts and customer data

Protect users and avoid avoidable technical liabilities.

WHEN TO DO THISBefore accepting private customer data, staff logins or real payments.ESTIMATED WORK TIMEDepends on integration complexity
↗
Your one job

Protect users and avoid avoidable technical liabilities.

01

Do this now

  1. 01

    Decide what information the website actually needs to collect. Do not store unnecessary sensitive details.

  2. 02

    Keep server-side API keys out of frontend code; use environment secrets, HTTPS and access controls.

  3. 03

    For databases, apply row-level or equivalent user isolation, validate inputs server-side, rate-limit public forms and check error/log exposure.

  4. 04

    Test with two distinct accounts to confirm neither can read or change the other's records; use a reputable payment provider rather than handling card data directly.

02

Copy this into ChatGPT

Replace anything in [square brackets] with your real business details. The prompt is a shortcut, not a substitute for the steps above.

READY-TO-USE PROMPT
Review this [STACK/REPO] for launch security. Check credential exposure, authentication, authorization, data access separation, HTTPS, secure payment redirects, input validation, rate limits, logging, backups and dependency vulnerabilities. Specify real tests to run and evidence needed before I can claim security is verified. Do not mark a control passed unless you inspected/tested it.
03

Finish with this

Security checklist and a verified account-isolation test report where applicable.

Before moving on, check your work against the following:

  • No production secrets exposed publicly
  • User/customer records are isolated when accounts exist
  • Payments handled by trusted provider
DON’T MAKE THIS MISTAKE

Putting service-role secrets in JavaScript or calling a dashboard secure without testing authorization.
